reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises for fcc FeCoNi. E1 shows carbon stabilizes the fcc phase in a different alloy but does not address coercivity or anisotropy. E2 reports coercivity enhancement in RTA-treated films via anisotropic strain, not interstitial carbon. E3 discusses carbon solubility and carbide formation in FeMnCoCr, not magnetic properties. None of the evidence demonstrates that interstitial carbon in single-phase fcc FeCoNi increases magnetocrystalline anisotropy or coercivity.
premises: Interstitial carbon can be retained in fcc FeCoNi without carbide precipitation at 1–2 wt%
Interstitial carbon induces lattice distortions and directional chemical ordering in fcc alloys
Such distortions and ordering enhance magnetocrystalline anisotropy
Enhanced anisotropy increases domain wall pinning and coercivity
Coercivity can rise from <100 Oe to 200–350 Oe in carbon-doped fcc FeCoNi
